subject: Post-demo recap: expected token profile, budget, and burst/overage terms
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Narang <priya@acme.io>, Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: expected token profile, budget, and burst/overage terms

Hi Priya / Mike,

Thanks again for your time earlier — appreciate the walkthrough of Acme Payments' authorization flows and the sample transcripts. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of the profile you shared:
- Active users (auth flows): ~120k/month, peak hourly concurrency during business hours ~1.2k
- Expected prompt+completion average: ~350 tokens per API call (mostly short prompts, longer system messages)
- Baseline steady-state volume: ~35M tokens/month
- Burst scenarios: automated batch jobs and holiday spikes could push to ~120M tokens/month for short windows (24-72h)
- Target unit economics: you called out a target in the $700–1,000 per 1M tokens range for production (goal: ~$800/1M for the committed tier)

Questions we promised to surface:
1) How Redwood handles short-term bursts above committed quota (soft burst vs throttling)
2) Overage unit price and whether overages are tiered or flat
3) Timeline and lead time for quota increases for Dedicated/Private options

Pricing/terms snapshot (high level, subject to formal quote):
- Committed tier (monthly commit): list price $1,100/1M tokens; typical committed discount brings effective $700–900/1M depending on commit size and contract term.
- Burst handling: hosted tiers allow temporary burst up to 3x committed sustained rate for up to 48 hours (soft cap behavior: requests accepted; latency SLO may degrade; we do not reject unless quota > 3x for >48h).
- Overage pricing: standard overage = 1.25x the effective committed rate; short-term extended bursts (beyond 48h) escalate to 1.5x until you normalize or increase quota.
- Quota increase lead time: for Hosted API, we can apply most increases within 24–72 hours; for Dedicated/Private, typical lead time is 7–14 days depending on GPU capacity and scale.

Attachments: I attached a quick token forecast template (acme-token-forecast.xlsx) populated from your numbers, and a pricing sketch (rdw-pricing-quote-v2.pdf) with three commitment bands.

Proposed next steps: 
- Priya/Mike: confirm whether the 120M short spikes are monthly cumulative or single-window peaks (quick reply ok)
- If committed tier is attractive, we can generate a draft quote and routing/SLAs to match (I can have that to you by EOD Friday if you confirm numbers)
- Alex (cc'd) can run a quick check on batching/kv-cache opportunities to drive the effective $/1M lower in practice; recommend a short technical sync (30 min) next week.

If there's anything to adjust in the forecast I attached, let me know — otherwise I’ll draft the quote and the proposed burst guardrail language for review.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0192


From: Priya Narang <priya@acme.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: expected token profile, budget, and burst/overage terms

Hi Soojin — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 120M figure refers to a single-window peak across a 48h holiday promotion (not cumulative across month). Typical off-peak weeks are closer to 25–30M.
- We’re aiming for procurement approval for a pilot at the $800/1M target. Pilot would cover 40–50M tokens/month for 2 months.
- Critical ask: what happens if we breach burst caps during our pilot (automated claim flows)? We cannot afford hard throttling during promos.

Questions: 
1) Is the 48h soft-burst guarantee (3x) written into the hosted terms or is it an operational policy? We need explicit language for the pilot quote.
2) If overage is billed at 1.25x, are those overage charges capped per event?

Happy to move forward with the pilot if the burst behavior is acceptable and the quote reflects the $800/1M target for the pilot band.

Best,
Priya
VP Product, Acme Payments
priya@acme.io

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Narang <priya@acme.io>, Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: expected token profile, budget, and burst/overage terms

Hi Priya — great, thanks for clarifying the single-window peak. Short answers below, then next steps.

Burst handling (short):
- The hosted soft-burst behavior (accept requests up to 3x committed sustained rate for up to 48h) is part of our operational policy and we will include explicit language in the pilot quote. That language can read: "Hosted: temporary burst allowance up to 3x committed sustained rate for a contiguous 48-hour window; overage tier pricing applies for sustained usage beyond that window. Redwood will provide rollbacks or throttling only when usage materially threatens overall region capacity."
- For pilot contracts we typically include a clause that gives Acme notice and escalation paths rather than immediate hard-throttle. We can include a one-time per-quarter event cap to protect against runaway usage if you prefer.

Overage pricing and event caps:
- Overage = 1.25x effective pilot rate by default. For burst events we can put a per-event cap (e.g., no more than 2x the committed monthly spend billed as overage for a single event) for the pilot; this is negotiable and should be in the quote.

Pilot pricing proposal (sketch):
- Pilot band: 40M/month commit for 2 months at a flat $800/1M tokens effective (billed monthly).
- Burst allowance: up to 120M single-window as you described (covered by soft-burst policy).
- Overage: 1.25x pilot rate after the 48h burst window; per-event billing cap = 2x monthly committed spend for the event for the pilot.
- If you exceed 3x committed sustained rate for >48h and do not sign an accelerated quota increase, charges escalate to 1.5x until normalized.

Next steps: 
1) If you confirm pilot band, I will generate a formal quote (DocuSign link) and include the explicit burst language and per-event cap.
2) Alex can join a 30-min tech sync to validate the forecast and advise on batching/kv cache (I’ll include a recommended config to lower your effective tokens per call).

I’ve attached the populated forecast and a draft sketch of the quote. If that sounds good I’ll send the formal quote by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: expected token profile, budget, and burst/overage terms

Hi Priya — quick technical note ahead of a short sync: 

- Based on the sample transcripts, a 10–15% reduction in effective tokens per call is achievable with prompt normalization and server-side prompt templates; that would move you closer to ~630–720 effective $/1M at the same list prices.
- For KV-cache and batching: our hosted runtime supports prefix caching for repeated system messages and continuous batching inside the same connection; we typically see 8–12% latency improvements and token savings when customers enable these patterns.
- Regarding surge protection: there are two mechanisms we recommend combined in pilot runs: soft-burst allowance (policy described by Soojin) plus a configurable token throttle rule that routes excess traffic to a best-effort fallback model variant to avoid hard failures. That fallback variant cost is lower but may have slightly different quality characteristics — we can define acceptable thresholds in the pilot.

I can be available Tues/Wed next week for a 30-min tech sync. Would you like a calendar invite now?

--
Alex Martinez
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
